feedback: Evidence base: iterations 0 to 2 all went off track on every trial (60/60 each). Scores were 30.8, 55.5 and 53.0. Max_error sat at 0.061 to 0.065 m, just over the 0.06 m floor. Line-loss events fell from 2 (iteration 0 and 1) to 1 (iteration 2, widened array with sensor_size 0.012). Widening the array and raising kp/kd did not stop the drift, so the sensor row position is the next lever to test. Read from the candidate: all five sensors move from y = 0.04 to y = 0.07 m, with x spacing, sensor_size 0.012, weights, kp 3.5, kd 0.3, base_speed 1.6 and last_direction all unchanged. That makes this a single-variable test of lookahead, which is the right test given iteration 2 ruled out sensor width as the main limit. Nothing here predicts its outcome. The changes below depend on what the next race shows. If max_error drops below 0.06 m and line_loss_events fall to 0 or 1, keep y = 0.07 and raise base_speed toward 2.0 for completion time. If max_error still exceeds 0.06 m with line loss at 1 or more, raise kd toward 0.5 to damp overshoot. If line-loss events stay near 1 or 2, test line_loss search_left or search_right. If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.15 while the robot stays on track, reduce kp toward 2.5 because the signal is now stronger at the front.
requested_changes: If max_error is below 0.06 m with line_loss_events 0 or 1 but runs do not finish: raise controller.base_speed from 1.6 toward 2.0, keeping sensor y = 0.07, since iteration 2 shows the line is now held and the 3 s limit needs about 1.5 m/s.

If max_error still exceeds 0.06 m with line_loss_events of 1 or more: raise controller.kd from 0.3 toward 0.5 to damp overshoot on bends, keeping the forward sensor row, since iterations 1 and 2 showed max_error stuck near 0.061 to 0.065 m at kd 0.3.

If line_loss_events stay near 1 to 2 after the sensor move: change controller.line_loss from 'last_direction' to 'search_left' or 'search_right', since no gain or width change so far has reduced the loss below 1 per run.
